title: I am, you are
subtitle: Unit 1: je suis, tu es, and tu or vous

steps.title: Je suis means I am
steps.body:
The verb être means to be. It changes with the person, so you learn the forms: je suis (I am), tu es (you are), il est (he is), elle est (she is).

Listen to the sounds. Tu es and il est are almost the same: ty-EH and eel-EH.

steps.explain: Je means I. Tu means you, and elle means she.
Il means he. Il est canadien means he is Canadian.

steps.title: Tu or vous?
steps.body:
French has two words for you. Use tu for one friend, a family member or a child. Use vous for one person you do not know well, for someone older, and in official places like an office or a clinic.

Vous also means you for more than one person. With vous, être becomes vous êtes.

In Québec people often start using tu sooner than in France. As a newcomer, vous is the safe choice with someone new.

examples.en: Are you Canadian? (to a stranger or an official)

steps.prompt: You meet your new landlord. Which word do you use for you?
steps.explain: Vous is polite and safe with someone you do not know.

steps.prompt: A friend your age asks you a question. Which word do you use for you?
steps.explain: Tu is for friends, family and children.

steps.title: Je parle, j'habite
steps.body:
Most French verbs end in -er, like parler (to speak) and habiter (to live). For je, remove -er and add -e: je parle, j'habite.

For tu, add -es: tu parles. For il or elle, add -e: elle parle. All three sound the same, because the last letters are silent. This is the silent-letter rule from Stage 0.

Before a vowel or a silent h, je becomes j': j'habite.

steps.prompt: How do you say You speak English to a friend?
steps.explain: Tu parles means you speak. Je parle is I speak, and il parle is he speaks.

steps.question: Who is Canadian?
steps.explain: Elle means she. Elle est canadienne means she is Canadian.

steps.question: Which word for you did you hear?
steps.explain: You hear vous êtes: voo-ZET. The s of vous links to êtes with a z sound.

steps.title: Next: a real conversation
steps.body: In the next lesson two neighbours meet in a hallway. You will hear everything you learned in this unit, in one short scene.
